segment.source: ::Tony and Marcus seem to be discussing something and are unaware of your presence.:: <end>
<end>

I gotta say I'm impressed with you, Marky. Not only did you *not* get zoned out, but you actually did somethin' useful during the fight. Sure, you played with your little toys from the safety of your tent, but hey - you got the job done.<end>

That is... a compliment, correct? And just for the record, the turrets *can* work autonomously; however, in situations such as this one it is always the wisest course of action to have someone behind the controls for better target assessment.<end>

No, no, no, Marky, no - no! How many times I gotta remind you? You gotta put it kinda like this: "Well, if it wasn't for me, you *pipeworker*, you'd be checkin' the pipes from your forehead right now." Yeeaah.
Where I'm from, you gotta pull out them hardcore comebacks, not go on about... you know, target assessment.<end>
Checking... the pipes?<end>

Oh, grind it. It's Core City slang, Marky. It means to take a leak, to piss. That whole phrase was supposed to mean that one of the freaks would've made a hole in my forehead and-- Okay, okay, forget the slang. Use your own words. Just not one of your la-di-da words like "urinatin'" or - oh, oh - "ejectin' bladderal liquid waste"! Oooh, oh.<end>
Don't be absurd, Tone, no one uses that expression. You just made that up.<end>

Well, it's how all you Northerners, fat rats and the rest of the la-di-das sound to me. You're too... uptight. ::He squishes his nose upward.:: You all sound like you're gonna get pipeworkin' cancer if you say a naughty word. You use far too many dumb, sterile euphemisms that suck all the fun outta language, Marky. So please, the next time you wanna go check the pipes, you're not *urinatin'* - but goin' for a piss!<end>

I see... I see where this is going. How about this: If it hadn't been for me and my turrets, you... no, your head would've been... impaled on a spear and... paraded around. Angrily. You... *stinker*.<end>
What. the. pipe--? No. *No*. ::He grabs his crotch.:: Ooooooow, ooow! You're so lame it hurts my... Ah...<end>

::While Tony is holding onto his crotch and acting out utter agony, Marcus is slowly squeezing his forehead into a chasmic frown. He erupts as soon as his irritation reaches its peak.::
How about I bust your nose to take your mind off your groin?<end>

Oooooooh... That's it, that's it! Yeah, yeah, yeah. You're gettin' the hang of it. Oh, I am glad you got at least some of it in you, Marky! There's still hope. Gimme another one. Come on, I wanna hear a hardcore insult...<end>
::[Intimidation]:: You wanna check your pipes? You'll be checking your windpipe instead after I've rammed my fist down your throat.<end>
Listen to this, Marcus! Now that's someone who's got it. Not only should the line be hardcore, but the delivery's gotta be spot on too! *RRNN*! You wanna make a guy soil his pants, all the way.<end>
Oh, you're... you're that new sec-trooper, eh...<end>
That's $(context.player.Name). $(context.playerArenaTitle). Invictus! Champion of the Arena.<end>
Nice to meet you, $(context.player.Name), I'm Marcus, Marcus Werther. I saw how you fought through the turrets' visual feed. Impressive. Unlike this blabbermouth here.<end>
You're gettin' the hang of it, Marky. Keep pokin'.<end>
Yes, well... Tell us, what do you need?<end>
<end>
I wanted to speak with you, Marcus.<end>
I wanted to speak with you, Tony.<end>
I don't need anything, actually. See you some other time.<end>
That's $(context.player.Name) - $(context.playerArenaTitle). Gladiator in the Arena!<end>
That's $(context.player.Name) - a true badass.<end>
::[Intelligence]:: You sound as intelligent as someone who's been sucking on a lead pacifier as an infant.<end>
Lead? Bwahahaha! Dominatin'! That pipeworkin' *hurts*, yo. But that's how you do it. That, my friend... is hardcore.<end>
::[Intelligence]:: If people compared my butt and your face, they'd think we're twins.<end>

Hardcore. Thanks!
There you go, Marcus. That one was simple and insultin'. You can easily start a fight with that one.<end>
::[Intelligence]:: Why are you grabbing your crotch, Ladelman? Another migraine?<end>
Not baaaad... Kinda lightweight, but it's decent.<end>
I iswill muchbroke ur waaitstik and boom ur mindkanta toso hardrecept totos.<end>
What? Is that...? Don't tell me you've actually listened to that derailed Norman dude? I don't even know what the sentence means. It's... gotta be somethin' absolutely perverse, though.<end>
Eat poo poo.<end>
Damn it, $(#man/woman), you're even lamer than him...<end>
::Say nothing.::<end>
Look, Tone, I don't-- ::Marcus finally notices you.:: <end>
Excuse me for interrupting...<end>
<end>
Excuse me for interrupting, but I need to talk to you, Marcus.<end>
Excuse me for interrupting, but I need to talk to you, Tony.<end>
::Listen to the conversation.::<end>
So, Marky... this is it. We're leavin' the Hell's Gut.<end>

::He nods.:: Yes, yes...
::Silence.::<end>
It was horrible.<end>
Pipeworkin'.<end>
Since we arrived here we've had to deal with bugs and giant serpents...<end>
Them toxic crap tubes!<end>
...disease, sickness...<end>
Dominated by stinkin' germs!<end>
Native attacks...<end>
Chalk zoners!<end>
Professor's kidnapping...<end>
Sea zoners!<end>
Food shortages...<end>
Pipeworkin' canned eels!<end>

But frankly, Tone, I really... ::He takes a deep breath.::
I really missed some hardcore grinding.<end>

::His eyes flare up.:: Bwahahahahaha! Bwahahahaha! That's the... oh, damn... that's what I wanted to hear from you, Marky! Unadulterated, straight-to-the-point *grindin'*! Bwahahahah!
::He looks up through a hole in the tent roof.:: If there is anythin' good about you, Hell's Gut, is that you made this man just a bit less la-di-da. Thank you, Hell's Gut - *thank you*!<end>
So... Lilly?<end>
::He shows his ring.:: Nope. Maria.<end>
Oh, well, as long as you're getting some... lovely lady posterior.<end>
Hm! You can sound cultured when you want to, eh, Tone?<end>

Hey, Tone ain't no bone, boy-eeeeah!
Just don't get too used to it.<end>
I'm actually going to miss you two.<end>
::He pauses for a moment.:: Uh... you know, $(context.npc_xpbl_ladelman_playerName), I was wonderin'... Can I get your autograph? That'd be so hardcore!<end>

::He pulls out a blood-spattered cheering glove with two extended fingers and "Arena" printed on it. You see a number of signatures on it: Bloodgod - written in blood - Mower, Zone-out, Decapito and others.::
This is my cheerin' glove. It had seen a lot. ::He hands you a black marker pen.::<end>
::Sign as Invictus.::<end>
Yeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeah! Dominatin'! Thank you so much! ::He looks at the glove again.:: Yeeeah...<end>
Now, as much as I like hangin' out with you two, <end>
I can't wait to get out of this pipeworkin' place. ::He cleans his forehead with a handkerchief and squeezes it by his side.:: Yeeeeah!<end>
Anything you need before the laborers start taking things out?<end>
::Sign as $(context.playerArenaTitle).::<end>
::Sign as $(context.player.Name).::<end>
I'm sorry, I don't do autographs.<end>
Well, uh, I guess if dominatin' in the Arena wasn't enough... ::He puts the marker pen away, sadly looks at the glove one more time before putting it away as well.::<end>
::Shake your head.::<end>
No.<end>
::He nods.:: <end>
Get a tent, you two lovebats.<end>
We would if we could, bwahahaha!<end>
I've frankly gotten sick of listening to you two. Glad it's finally over.<end>
Well, to tell you the truth, we've also gotten sick of watchin' you starin' at us from the doorway like a retard, bwahahaha!<end>
Well, folks, don't know about you, but <end>
Pirates...<end>

Pipeworkin' *drop-off*! ::He clenches his fists, stops, then bows and shakes his head - all of this contained within a single second, as if vacillating between distress and aggression.::
He can't freakin' do this! He can't keep me in 'ere like a, like a rat!<end>
Calm down, Tone, calm down. We got a situation and are trying to keep everything under control.<end>

It's 'cause I'm a Southerner, right? Huh? ::His erratic gesticulation continues.::
But of course, we're all double-dealin' ratters, ain't we? Well I'll give 'im a pipe--<end>
Hey! Don't do anything stupid! You'll just make it worse for yourself. <end>
I did nothin' wrong! Swear - *swear* on my sister Lilly!<end>

I know that. But Chief Briggs doesn't. We have to check everything and everyone.
I got you covered. I *got* you covered. Now stop yapping and calm down.<end>

::He stop for a moment, then raises his index finger in the air.:: I was once thrown in jail by the Praetorians, you know. I flung crap at 'em! ::He gestures the whole motion, complete with wrinkling his nose from the disgusting smell.::
They locked me into solitary for a few days, sure, but I showed them who's TONY LADELMAN!<end>
I know, I know. You told me about that twice already. That's why I'm trying to stop you from doing something like that again.<end>

Oh, I'd hit Briggs right in 'is... *ugh*! ::He grabs a wrench and just throws it in anger. Coincidentaly, he threw it in your general direction, almost hitting you in the head.::
$(context.npc_xpbl_ladelman_playerName)! Damn! Sorry!<end>
Take it easy, man.<end>
$(context.player.Name). Now's not the time. <end>
I'll take care of him, and you... you come back later, okay?<end>
Got it.<end>
::Leave without saying anything.::<end>

Chief Briggs wants to see you. He's in the Keep, by the evacuation tunnels.
Go.<end>
I'll go see him straight away.<end>
I'm not Briggs!<end>
Watch it, you dimwit!<end>
::Pick it up and throw it at him.::<end>
::He ducks and the wrench flies over his head and hits the boxes in the back.::<end>

::He looks at both of you.:: Stop it!
::Then he focuses just on you.:: <end>
So, Marky, now that we've got access to the Keep, what's down there?<end>

Well, I've yet to go there myself, but from what I understand the ground level contains a lot of fried equipment and an elevator, while the lower level has a few offices and access to what seem to be shelters and evacuation tunnels. The elevator won't descend further, so who knows, maybe there is a vast military installation down there, just like Professor Oldfield had thought.<end>
But despite all of this, there is a lot to discover. Seeger's working on recovering the data from the computers, the dusters are sorting the personal items and <end>
the sec-medics are <end>
inspecting the bodies of NFT soldiers. It seems they were neutralized with mutagen gas and... well... it is a grisly scene.<end>
Mutagen, eh? Zoned 'em out with mutagen. Guess the Biocorp has been in the mutatin' business for a long, long time.<end>

It appears so. It was Seeger who told me that, actually, and... he told me they killed each other. Before, um, disintegrating. The soldiers. He, you know, he conveyed the disgusting image pretty well, and you know how squeamish he is.<end>
Wimp.<end>

Those men, they must've died in great pain, but what they were while they were still alive... that seems even scarier. ::He pauses.:: Now that I think of it, there aren't many things worse than being turned into a... an agonized monstrosity, mauling in blind rage the people you've fought alongside of, your brothers, friends and comrades, only to join them afterwards... one piece at a time.<end>

Hey, Marky, listen... Us Southerners pretty much live with mutants here. We got Old Junkyard, we got 'em lurkin' in all these facilities all over the South - we even got them in Core City sewers. Damn, Marky - they're in the sewers! You could travel to Core City by ferry, take a wrong turn 'cause one stupid zoner misdirected you and end up bein' zoned out by tumorous people that bathe in what the city had eaten and zoned out the day before.<end>

Look, it's obvious, man, Seeger's story has gotten to ya. The way you talk about it... I can tell. What I'm tryin' to say here... is don't think about it too much. Oh, the nasty, hardcore things I've seen in life... heh.<end>
It hasn't gotten to me... I'm just...<end>

Hey, man, listen to your Tone: I was but a little Junkyard kid, yeeeaah, way before I moved to Core City, when I had a close encounter with... a horrible beast. Horrible! It was a huge, fat, gross, deformed creature. I was in the shack with Jumbo, my six-month old brother who was sleeping on the ol' sofa... when *it* came through the door. ::He makes a sweeping motion.:: Bam! Opened the door. I froze - it was on *fire*. Its single good eye - the other was long gone - was chokin' me with burnin' anger. Yeah - it wanted my blood.
And all I could do was stand there, paralyzed, and watch...<end>
::He stares at Ladelman in silence, consumed by the story.::<end>

It closed the distance in an instant and my eyes went up as it stood before me. It grasped me with its big, hairy, oily hands and lifted me up in the air. And as it roared at me... I managed to scream these words...<end>
::Marcus is not blinking.::<end>
"No, Uncle Dave, it wasn't me who broke your drill - it was Jumbo!"<end>
Oh, I should have seen it coming...<end>

In retrospect, I shouldn't have said Jumbo, 'cause Jumbo couldn't raise his own butt let alone an HD-999 drill. Sadly, Jumbo never made it to raisin' his butt at all, as he died from pneumonia a few months later. Anyway, Uncle Dave gave me such a brutal spankin' I didn't *dare* touch, look or even think about his tools. Not even after a train zoned 'im out.<end>
I thought we were talking about mutants?<end>
You should've seen how ugly that man was. He's my uncle, but damn, that face is hardcore.<end>

::He starts laughing, lowering his head while still leaning on the table.::
You know what's going through my head right now? Maybe we should stop trying to learn more about NFT and instead focus on that crazy mind of yours. I bet we'd learn more interesting things than anything this place could offer.<end>
Deep, man. But you wanna know what's even deeper?<end>
What?<end>
Do one-eyed people blink or wink?<end>
Well, that's... hmmm...<end>
Yeah! It's been on my mind ever since I told you the story. Remember, my uncle had one eye.<end>
What do you think, $(context.player.Name)? Do one-eyed people blink or wink?<end>
<end>
It's the same thing.<end>
Blink or wink? That's what we wanna hear.<end>
Winking is just "blinking with meaning" anyway, so I'd say blink.<end>
Ah, but it's only got meanin' when you got both eyeballs. But if you only got one... then how do you know? <end>
It's one mind-dominatin' question, right?<end>
Let's leave this for some other time. We're going a bit too far with this. I'm sure $(context.player.Name) came here for some other, more important reason.<end>
Am I correct?<end>
You wink with a single eye, so I'd say wink.<end>

But they're also blinkin', 'cause that's the only eye they got, so technically they're lubricatin' *all* of their eyes at the same time. Winkin' is closin' and openin' of a single eye, but in this case, so is blinkin'. <end>
It can be both, depending on the context.<end>
I see your point, and *technically* you're right, but ain't every blink a wink as well? Uh, *technically*, in this case? <end>

::[Biology]:: Blinking is an involuntary action while winking is subject to conscious control. So if only the palpebral portion of the orbicularis oculi muscle is engaged, then a person is blinking; if the orbital portion of the muscle is engaged as well, then it is a conscious action and is a wink, for it is most likely but not exclusively used to convey some meaning. There.<end>
Wow... I don't even know how to respond to this. You're... right, I guess, but ain't supposed to bring *actual* knowledge into these kinds of discussions.<end>
On a side note, if the palpebral portion, upper, is relaxed while the orbital, lower, is contracted - then you're pretty much squinting.<end>
::He squints while keeping his mouth open. Then he smiles.:: Ye-he-he-heah... I get it, I get it. Hardcore!<end>
That settles it, then. Anyway, what do you need?<end>
::[Intelligence]:: They bwink.<end>
Ha! I like it. I like it! Bwinkin'. Bwinkin'... hmmm... That's the one. I'll remember that.<end>
I have no idea.<end>
Come on, think about it.<end>
No idea. I've got better things to worry about.<end>
Of course, don't mind us. What did you need?<end>
Doc Savage is <end>
Tone, you mentioned you had a sister.<end>

Yes, Lilly, my little sis. There were six of us, mhm, but by the time I was thirteen, only Lilly and me were still alive. She was barely three then, so she don't remember the rest of 'er siblings.<end>
I'm sorry to hear that. I've read that child mortality is high here in the South.<end>

You betcha. That's the reason moms here pump out so many kids, unlike yours which are done after one or two. Then it's legs closed and: ::He switches to falsetto voice.:: "Get your filthy hands offa me, zoner." Bwahahaha!<end>

Well, North Underrail has much better living conditions, so it is likely that all our children will reach reproductive age, hence the smaller number of children per family. Here, it's obviously different.<end>

But that is why our kids grow up hardcore. Life here ain't free - you gotta earn it. Work for it. Dominate it. Yeeeah. YEAH! Survival of the hard... core... *hardcorest*. And you get wimps 'cause they get life for free.<end>
I beg to differ... but let's not get into that. Do you keep in touch with Lilly?<end>
Yeah. We see each other from time to time. She's a high-profile rod grinder, so she's a busy girl.<end>
Rod grinder? Um, construction work?<end>
No, man, no - she grinds rods: She's a hooker! Zone me out and spit on my corpse, do you not have prostitutes in North Underrail?<end>
Not in Dis! B-but nonetheless, uh, how could I have known what the words mean, Tone? It's your stupid slang.<end>

Hey! I could hook you up with her once we're back in Core City. You look like you could use someone dominatin' your rod *real* good. Yeah, baby. I'll even arrange for a discount. Only for the best of my pals.<end>
Damn it, Tone, you're insane! I'm m-m-married.<end>
Oooooh, you're gonna forget you're *m-m-m*-married after you see my little sis and her massive--<end>
Tone...<end>
Listen, you wimp! Lilly's ain't no cheap ska--<end>
I'm married, you fool! See... s-see this ring? Where I'm from this means I love my wife.<end>
You Northerners and your stupid rings. You're a man - and you have a man's needs. And a rod. And Mary-Ann ain't here--<end>
It's *Maria*.<end>
There you go... You've already forgotten 'er name.<end>
No, no, no. It's you who remembered it wrong! D-damn it, I'm not having... intercourse with your sister.<end>
Bwahahaha. "Intercourse." La-di-da, ain't we polite. At least you didn't say "rub our bodies romantically against one another." It's dominatin' grindin', man. Say it!<end>
::He sighs.:: Can we... change the topic?<end>
Ah, no, no, no. Not while you're feelin' *this* uncomf--<end>
$(context.player.Name)! You're here. Wh-what do you need?<end>
About this Boggy person...<end>
Yeah, yeah. Boggy's one derailed maniac from Junkyard. Heard of it? Junkyard?<end>
No.<end>
Well, Marky, you need to brush up on your geography. Junkyard is one of the capitals of anarchy here in South Underrail. And they've got a mutant zoo. You shouldn't feed the mutants, though.<end>

Anyways, Boggy's one of the Scrapper hitmen I once fixed a scrap compactor for. Long and irrelevant story that is, but what I wanna tell you about is his wicked sense of humor. The guy looked hardcore all the way. Got this big scar over his gray, lifeless eye, jawline you could cut yourself on, shoulders wide as a train. To make 'im even more scary, he had these two doberman dogs, Bolt and Snap. Stupid names, but it ain't stupid no more when he lets them loose on your ass.<end>
I hope this doesn't turn into one of your morbid tales.<end>
Shut up. ::He smiles.::<end>

So - Bolt and Snap, like their master, are scary as burnin' hell. And they're this big, look... ::He spreads his arms wide and looks between them with a mean face.:: Yeeeeeah, this big, man. They will strip the flesh from your bones faster than them chomper fishes - but only if Boggy gives them the order. They are so well-trained you could put a baby in their mouth and go out and get derailed with your woman, knowin' that your kid's in safe jaws.<end>
That's... an interesting way to put it.<end>

That's life, Marky. But these dogs are like machines. Now, Boggy taught them a certain command: When he points to someone and says, "Chomp on them cobbles, boys!" they'd charge that person, salivatin' and snappin' their jaws like the true harbingers of castration. But - it's a trick! They just knock folks to the ground and keep 'em pinned down while Boggy's dyin' from laughter. He just orders them back once he's had enough.<end>

Marky, I've seen so much death, sufferin' and misery durin' my lifetime it'd make a wimp like you sick. But the looks of horror I saw on the faces of those poor pipeworkers that were the victims of Boggy's perverse sense of humor eclipses everythin' I've ever witnessed. Some turn pale, some check the pipes in their pants, some try to run, one even fainted! There was also a guy that yelled, "But I still need mine!" Bwahaha! What a zoner.<end>
Horrible! How can you possibly laugh at something like that?<end>
How can you *not* laugh? It's a prank, Marky! It's fun. Like, like, tazin' someone while they're checkin' the pipes, or pourin' laxatives into people's food.<end>
Would you still find it funny if Boggy did that to you?<end>
Ha - he did it! The first time I came to fix his scrap compactor.<end>
And?<end>
I was the one that yelled I still needed mine.<end>
Tone...<end>

Bwahahaha! Marky, I've been pranked all my life. I've been brutalized, dominated and made fun of in every imaginable way. Sure, I got scared when those dogs charged at my hangin' twins, I'll be honest, but I found the whole thing so hilarious that I laughed with Boggy afterward. It's what life is all about. Not livin' in a bubble. And after your skin becomes thick enough, nothin', and I mean nothin' can break through no more. You become - hardcore. While you, Marky, you were all traumatized when I tazed you in the toilet.<end>
My leg got lodged in the hole!<end>
Well, the next time I do it you're gonna laugh and say, "Oh, you cheeky pipeworker!"<end>
There isn't going to be next time. There. isn't.<end>
Mhm. MHM.<end>
By the way, why does Boggy have a scrap compactor?<end>
Eh... Hey, there's $(context.npc_xpbl_ladelman_playerName).<end>
$(context.player.Name).<end>
So, Marky, tell me about this wife of yours.<end>
Maria?<end>
Well, unless you have more than one, then yes, Mary-An-- Marya... Maria.<end>

::Marcus flashes a smile of reminiscence and begins his story.:: I met her at the University of Dis during my studies. I was studying military technology - weapons engineering - and she was at the IT, yet for some wonderful reason we kept running into each other despite the fact that our...<end>

That's hardcore, Marky, but - I'm not tryin' to say your story is borin', it's hardcore, really - but I was more interested in knowin' more about... her. Go straight for the important bits and leave the introduction for some other time.<end>
Oh. Well, as I have said already, she studied molecular biology. Now, her parents are the well-known...<end>

Marky, when I say I want to know more about a woman - and often women in general - I don't mean, like, you dig, about where she studied or what 'er job is, or even how well-cooked she likes 'er steak - although that does come in handy later on.<end>
::Marcus gives him a blank stare.::<end>

You don't dig it yet? Marky, pay attention: What is the first thing you think of when you see a woman walkin' by? You surely ain't thinkin', "Oh, I wonder what kind of a person she is?" or, "Oh, does she watch the Gauntlet?", or even, "Does she like her steaks well-done or medium-rare?".
What? I like steaks...<end>
::Marcus' gaze persists.::<end>

You *assess* her. Four points of interest: face, mammaloons, ass and legs. In that order. From top to bottom. Some like it differently, but I like it this way. Top to bottom. Whatever the order, that's what *men* care about, not whether your kids are gonna make it past their third birthday. So when I ask you about your woman, I wanna hear about the important bits... of her, he-he.<end>
::His stare remains unchanged.::<end>
You must've noticed somethin', damn it. You married her.<end>
::He sighs.::<end>
You... you ain't into men by any chance? And Marry-Ann's just coverin' for ya? You said no to Lilly, and she's one domi--<end>
Tone! Tone. Tone - I get it. You want to know how... hot my wife is. I get it.<end>
Thank you. Thank you! He gets it, oh. Go ahead then, Marky.<end>
My wife is a beautiful woman.<end>
Okay. And?<end>
There is nothing more to say. She is beautiful in all respects.<end>
Four points of interest, Marky...<end>
Tone, have you ever been married?<end>
No, damn it, *no*! And what does that--<end>
How many women have you been with so far?<end>
::He displays a wide, proud smile.:: With enough to repopulate two North Underrails! Bwahahahaha!<end>
And have you ever loved any one of them?<end>
Uh, yeah, sure.<end>
"Yeah, sure"?<end>
Marky, what does this--<end>
Please answer me.<end>
Love is a... Well, maybe it's a strong word. I loved bein' around 'em... and in 'em. ::He grins.:: But them - eh! ::He shrugs.:: I cared for them.<end>

You see, Tone, you are too focused on the most superficial, primal, sexual things. When you spend enough time with women, quality time, men turn their attention to... different, more mature things. I do not ignore female beauty - I am a man too, you know. My heart has raced far too many times in the presence of gorgeous women.<end>

However, you see different things once you really get to know a person, and those soon become far more important than her breast size and the firmness of her posterior. And if those things are sufficient in quality, one might ignore one's partner's physical appearance altogether. And should, as age will chew and spit it out sooner than you think.<end>
Again with the euphemisms, Marky. You're doin' it on purpose now, right?<end>

My wife likes her steak rare. That's too rare for me, but hey, that's the way she eats it, and that is how I prepare it for her. And there are many other things about her I could tell you that have nothing to do with her appearance. Wonderful things, things that made me marry her in the first place.<end>
You cook for your wife!?<end>

Yes. What I am getting at here, Tone, is that your complete inability to... even fathom that something like this is possible and that men can appreciate these things makes me feel that you've never really felt... anything like it; had you, you would've understood me, and understood me well. But as things are, I am certain that you haven't spent enough time with a woman to get that far in a relationship, right?<end>
Marky...<end>
Listen, you... *wimp*!<end>
What? Hey, don't you be usin' my language against me, Marky!<end>
Everyone can thrust, but women stay with those who can really please them, and not only in the way you think.<end>
::Silence.::<end>
